title: Senior Research Engineer - Scientific AI
description:
Senior Research Engineer - Scientific AI


Newton Colmore is proud to be supporting a highly ambitious technology company that is developing an entirely new imaging capability. Their technology has the potential to reveal the internal structure of complex objects that conventional inspection methods struggle to see, creating applications across aerospace, energy, advanced manufacturing and national infrastructure.


We are assisting them in their search for an expert engineer to help build the machine learning and reconstruction systems at the heart of the platform. The challenge sits at the intersection of physics, simulation, AI and real-world engineering, and the role can be tailored, from senior engineer through to department head.


In terms of the challenge, every day you will work on problems that have no established answer.


You will develop AI systems capable of transforming complex data into accurate three-dimensional reconstructions, combining modern machine learning with first-principles physics.


You will have the freedom to own major technical decisions, influence architecture from day one and work closely with a small team solving incredibly complex problems.


Regarding the day-to-day, it should be a role where no one day would be the same, but here are some general responsibilities of the role;

  • Developing advanced machine learning models to reconstruct spatial information from large-scale sensor datasets.
  • Building graph neural networks and point-cloud based architectures for signal interpretation and track reconstruction
  • Creating physics-informed AI systems that combine learned models with mechanistic understanding.
  • Developing differentiable simulation frameworks that support both training and inference.
  • Designing uncertainty-aware reconstruction methods with robust confidence estimation.
  • Building end-to-end pipelines spanning simulation, training, validation and deployment.
  • Working with GPU and HPC infrastructure to solve computationally demanding challenges.


We are looking for expert engineers, and with the nature of this type of role, a lot of the time, it's difficult to pinpoint the exact profile needed. In short, that means the role can be tailored to the right person, but in terms of fundamentals, here are some of the attributes we are looking for;

  • Machine learning domain knowledge for scientific, industrial or engineering applications.
  • Computational imaging, inverse problems or reconstruction algorithms, ideally.
  • Graph Neural Networks, geometric deep learning or point-cloud processing.
  • Physics-informed machine learning experience.


Experience with complex sensor systems, simulation environments, high-performance computing or scientific instrumentation would be particularly valuable, but curiosity and problem-solving ability matter just as much.


It's an exciting company, developing a novel technology, and in terms of the package that is built around that, they offer the change to work autonomously, leaning on the leadership team whenever you need, with tailored salaries, equity, access to world-class compute infrastructure, and much more.


For obvious reasons, further details regarding the company, technology and applications will be discussed on a confidential basis with suitable candidates. Please do get in touch, or make an application, and a member of our team will be in touch.
